target_customer: Home health, hospice and personal-care agencies (post-acute care providers)
problem: Post-acute agencies lose revenue to denials and manual referral-to-cash work (intake, eligibility, authorization, reconciliation).
business_model: B2B SaaS / AI revenue-cycle platform for post-acute providers
product_category: AI revenue cycle management for post-acute care

founders.name: Kevin Calcado
founders.background_notes: Also SVP of Revenue roles at unnamed healthcare/tech companies per YC page.

founders.name: Jayen Ram (JJ)
founders.background_notes: Four-time startup engineering veteran: two health tech, one construction tech, one document AI company (unnamed).

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with payer portals, eligibility and authorization workflows plus ML denial prediction; standard engineering with hard integration parts for a small team in 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow depth and agency integrations could create lock-in, but no source shows proprietary data or regulatory position; many RCM vendors and AI entrants can copy the pitch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent RCM vendors such as Waystar were already publishing AI-for-post-acute-RCM content in 2025; no acquisition or copying of Claim Health found.

market_need_then: Company cites a $400B post-acute market and $20B+ annual revenue leakage (company claim, unverified); trade press in 2025 describes 15-20% first-pass home health claim denials (vendor blog, unverified).

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name tied to the product, no sourced evidence of brand pull or community.

outcome_analysis: Claim Health is early and active. It finished YC Spring 2025, reported about 30x revenue growth within a year (company claim) and raised a $4.4M seed in January 2026 led by Maverick Ventures. Founders have revenue and healthtech experience. Too early to judge success; the main risks are incumbents' AI features and long agency sales cycles, but no outcome evidence exists yet.
notes: Seed confirmed by Pulse 2.0 and HIT Consultant (BusinessWire release returned 403, not worked around). One aggregator lists $4.5M total, unverified. Dealroom EV estimate $18-26M unverified, not recorded. No dated competitor sources near the batch; a later aggregator names Medusind, FinThrive, Rivet but is not dated to 2025-04, so not listed. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Revenue growth is self-reported.
